title: Cleaning tools, solutions and preventing cross-contamination
audience: Cleaning staff who prepare solutions and use mops, cloths and buckets in healthcare areas.
learningOutcomes: Describe the routine care needed for mops, cloths and cleaning solutions.
Explain how colour coding reduces cross-infection.
Explain why a tool gets dried or replaced before its next use.

instruction.heading: Keeping the solution clean
instruction.body: Any cleaning plan has to stop solutions and tools turning into sources of contamination. Solutions are made up each day, or as often as required, and refreshed on the facility's timetable. A bucket that serves several rooms can move organisms from one room to the next.

instruction.heading: Mops and cloths
instruction.body: Mops and cloths get washed and air-dried before they are reused. Disposable heads and cloths are the other route. A cloth that returns to the bucket unrinsed and undried can deposit organisms on the next surface, so it is processed as the facility method describes.

instruction.heading: Colour coding
instruction.body: Facilities rely on checklists, colour-coded equipment, cleaning manuals and model contracts to keep standards consistent. Colour coding lowers the chance of carrying organisms between areas, because each colour is reserved for a defined area or task. Learn the colour scheme for your site before you start, and never take a coloured cloth into a different zone.

instruction.heading: New tools under review
instruction.body: Some newer methods, like microfibre cloths made to very fine standards and mists of hydrogen peroxide, may eventually cut down chemical reliance. Their effectiveness against different microbes, and their dependability across daily routines, still lacks solid proof. Only adopt such methods with a facility's sign-off in writing.

procedure: Check the colour scheme for the area and select the matching cloths and bucket.
Mix the detergent mix to the label, for the day or as the facility requires.
Use a clean cloth on the first surface, and rinse or change the cloth as the policy directs.
After the room is done, wash the mop head and cloths and leave them to dry before putting them away or reusing them.
Replace the solution when it is dirty or when the policy interval has passed.
Keep tools in a tidy, dry location away from clean linen and stock.

workedExamples.situation: You have finished a bathroom and now need to clean a patient's bedside area. You have one bucket and one cloth left.
workedExamples.reasoning: Change the solution and the cloth before working on the bedside area. Carrying a bathroom's soil and organisms into the patient area is the cross-contamination the guideline wants you to prevent.

equipmentAndPpe: Disposable mop heads, if the facility supplies them

commonErrors.error: Using the same bucket of solution for many rooms without changing it.
commonErrors.prevention: Change the solution according to policy, and sooner if it is visibly dirty.

commonErrors.error: Putting a wet cloth away without drying it.
commonErrors.prevention: Clean and dry the cloth or mop head before storing or reusing it.

commonErrors.error: Using a coloured cloth in an area it is not assigned to.
commonErrors.prevention: Follow the colour code exactly for each zone.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Only use the newer technologies named in the guideline, such as ultramicrofibre cloths or hydrogen peroxide mist, where the facility has approved them. They are not established as routine methods.

qualityStandard: Solution is mixed and changed on the schedule the facility sets.
Cloths and mop heads are dried or replaced after use.
Colour-coded equipment is used only in its assigned zone.
documentationEvidence: Record of equipment replaced or cleaned when the shift closes
summary: Solutions are mixed and replaced regularly, because a dirty solution spreads what it carries.
Mops and cloths are cleaned and dried, or replaced with single-use items.
Colour coding keeps zones separate; follow the site code exactly.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why are cleaning solutions replaced frequently in a healthcare setting?
options: Because the solution loses its colour on the trolley over time.
Because a used solution can carry organisms from one area to the next.
Because the manufacturer only allows one use per day.
Because the colour of the solution must be kept consistent.

knowledgeChecks.question: What is an acceptable way to deal with a used mop head?
options: Store it wet in the cupboard until the next day and then use it again
Wash it, dry it fully, then reuse it; or fit a fresh disposable head.
Rinse it briefly under the tap and use it in the next room.
Leave it in the bucket so it stays damp and use it for the next floor

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the purpose of colour coding in cleaning?
options: To make the equipment look more professional and to match the staff uniforms
To lower the odds of moving organisms between areas by tying each piece of equipment to a zone.
To show which cleaner has been allocated to the room and the time they arrived each day
To tell the cleaner which product to use on the floor and the product for the walls too

sourceReferences: Australian Guidelines for Prevention and Control of Infection in Healthcare, B1.4.2 (cleaning implements and solutions; checking systems); rights: not held by user; reworded (no copying)
